PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-09-17
37F, outpatient consultation for symptom evaluation.

S:
Patient presents for consultation regarding several weeks of joint aches in the hands and wrists with morning stiffness, intermittent low-grade fatigue, and a sun-sensitive facial rash. Denies chest pain. She reports the symptoms wax and wane and are worse after sun exposure. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. She works as a dental hygienist. Appetite is fair. Lives with her partner. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 118/74, HR 76, RR 14, Temp 98.3 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 150 lb, BMI 24.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: mild redness over sun-exposed skin of the face.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: mild tenderness at the wrists and small joints of the hands, no effusion, full range of motion.
Skin: faint sunburn-like redness over the cheeks.
Labs (this week): Hgb 11.7 g/dL, A1c 6.0%, ANA negative, urinalysis unremarkable.

A/P:
1. Rule out lupus; ANA negative. Facial redness fits sun exposure and the joint aches fit repetitive hand use; no further autoimmune testing or rheumatology referral needed. Advised strict sun protection.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron daily with vitamin C. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
4. Supportive care: discussed joint protection and pacing of hand-intensive tasks at work, along with over-the-counter measures for comfort.

Return in 3 months, sooner if the rash spreads or new joint swelling develops.
